title: Design exercise: SAA-4.4-S03
scenario: Halloran Transcription Services runs audio-processing workers in private subnets across three Availability Zones, and all outbound traffic leaves through one NAT gateway in the first zone. About 60 TB a month passes through it: 55 TB to Amazon S3 buckets in the same Region, 3 TB to Amazon DynamoDB and 2 TB to a partner's dictionary API that exists only on the public internet. A further 9 TB a month is copied to a second Region for a reporting cluster an analyst team built years ago; no residency rule or latency need requires it to live there. Workers in the other two zones account for two thirds of the traffic reaching the NAT gateway.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Finance targets cutting the bytes processed by NAT gateways by at least 90 percent
An outage in one Availability Zone must not cut partner-API access for workers in the other two zones
The reporting team accepts running its cluster in the primary Region

rubric.label: Bytes processed by NAT gateways fall by at least 90 percent of today's 60 TB a month, and the record identifies what remains and why it must still use that path
No worker traffic crosses an Availability Zone boundary to reach a NAT gateway, an outage in one zone leaves the other two with partner-API access, and the 9 TB a month no longer crosses Regions

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
